question: U Tirot Sing was a tribal chief who led a fierce resistance against the British attempts to build roads through his territory in which region?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tirot Sing was a chief of the Khasi tribe and one of the prominent leaders who resisted British colonial expansion in northeast India.
 
• He opposed the British plan to construct a road through his territory in the Khasi Hills, which was seen as an attempt to strengthen their control.
 
• In 1829, Tirot Sing initially agreed to allow the road construction but revoked his consent upon realizing the British’s ulterior motives of annexation.
 
• He led an armed revolt against the British forces, utilizing guerrilla warfare tactics in the difficult terrain of the Khasi Hills.
 
• Tirot Sing was eventually captured and deported to Dhaka (now in Bangladesh), where he died in captivity on July 17, 1835. He is regarded as a hero in Meghalaya and is remembered annually on his death anniversary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mizoram Hills**

 
 
• The Mizoram Hills, also known as the Lushai Hills, are located in the state of Mizoram in northeast India.
 
• These hills are home to the Mizo people, who have their unique culture and traditions.
 
• Historically, the Mizos were known for their fierce resistance against external influences, but their resistance was primarily against British incursions during the late 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Naga Hills**
 
 
• The Naga Hills are located in Nagaland and parts of Manipur in northeast India.
 
• The region is inhabited by the Naga tribes, who also resisted British incursions during the colonial era.
 
• Key resistance movements against the British included battles led by Naga warriors such as Rani Gaidinliu.
 
 
 
• **Lushai Hills**
 
 
• The Lushai Hills refer to the same region as the Mizoram Hills and are characterized by dense forests and rugged terrain.
 
• The British annexed the area in the late 19th century following military campaigns to suppress tribal uprisings.
 
• The hills are significant for their unique biodiversity and the cultural heritage of the Mizo people.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme**
 
 
• The question highlights the resistance movements against British colonial rule by tribal leaders in northeast India.
 
• Such revolts were often fueled by the British’s attempts to expand their control through infrastructure projects, which threatened tribal autonomy.
 
• The leaders like Tirot Sing are celebrated for their bravery and contribution to preserving their people’s culture and independence.
